what.heading: What is Keep Awake?
what.body: Keep Awake is a free, browser-based tool that prevents your screen from dimming, locking, or going to sleep. It uses the built-in Screen Wake Lock API, so there’s nothing to install and nothing runs in the background. Just open the page, turn it on, and your display stays lit for as long as you need.

items.title: Instant, no install
items.description: Works right in your browser. No downloads, accounts, or permissions to grant.

items.title: Private by design
items.description: Everything runs locally on your device. No tracking, no data leaves your browser.

items.title: Precise timers
items.description: Set an exact duration or keep it on forever. Countdowns stay accurate even when throttled.

items.title: Battery-friendly
items.description: Only the display stays on. No CPU-heavy tricks or fake activity in the background.

items.title: Works everywhere
items.description: Laptops, desktops, tablets, and phones, on any modern browser with Wake Lock support.

items.title: Easy on the eyes
items.description: Dark by default with a light theme, tuned for long sessions and dim rooms.

items.title: Downloads & uploads
items.description: Keep transfers going without the screen sleeping and pausing your session.

items.title: Coding & AI sessions
items.description: Watch builds, logs, or long-running AI tasks without touching the mouse.

items.title: Presentations & reading
items.description: Slides, dashboards, recipes, and sheet music stay visible, hands-free.

steps.title: Pick a duration
steps.description: Choose Always On, a preset, or set a custom time.

steps.title: Flip the switch
steps.description: Turn on Keep Awake. Your browser may ask you to confirm.

steps.title: Leave the tab open
steps.description: Keep this tab visible. It pauses if hidden and resumes when you return.

items.question: Is Keep Awake free?
items.answer: Yes. It’s completely free, with no account and no ads that follow you around.

items.question: Does it work if I switch tabs or minimize the window?
items.answer: No. Browsers only allow a wake lock while the tab is visible. If you switch away or minimize, it pauses and then resumes automatically when you come back.

items.question: Will it drain my battery?
items.answer: It only keeps the display awake, which uses some power like any lit screen. It doesn’t run heavy background work, so the impact is minimal.

items.question: Which browsers are supported?
items.answer: Recent versions of Chrome, Edge, and Safari support the Screen Wake Lock API. Older browsers may fall back to a lightweight video method or may not be supported.

items.question: Is any of my data collected?
items.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your settings are stored on your device and never sent anywhere.

timer.heading: Timer
timer.intro: A countdown and stopwatch that keeps your screen awake while it runs. Set a simple countdown, cycle work and rest rounds, ring a bell at intervals, or just track elapsed time.

items.title: Focus sessions
items.description: Run work/rest rounds while you code, write, or study, screen included.

items.title: Workouts
items.description: Interval training with a bell every round, no phone lock screen interrupting you.

items.title: Cooking & breaks
items.description: A simple countdown for the kitchen, a break, or anything else on the clock.

steps.title: Pick a mode
steps.description: Countdown (Simple, Interval, or Bell) or Stopwatch, from Settings.

steps.title: Set your time
steps.description: Enter hours, minutes, and seconds, or rounds for Interval.

steps.title: Press start
steps.description: The timer runs and keeps your screen awake until you pause or it finishes.

items.question: What's the difference between Interval and Bell?
items.answer: Interval alternates full Work and Rest periods for a set number of rounds, like a classic workout timer. Bell counts down one total duration and rings periodically along the way, without splitting into separate phases.

items.question: Does the timer keep my screen awake?
items.answer: Yes, starting the timer keeps your screen on for as long as it runs, the same Screen Wake Lock used by the rest of the site.

items.question: Will it still ring if I switch tabs?
items.answer: The countdown keeps accurate time in the background, but browsers can throttle inactive tabs, so the display and sound may lag slightly until you return to the tab.

items.question: Can I turn off the sound?
items.answer: Yes, toggle Alarm Sound off in Settings. It has no effect on Stopwatch, which never plays a sound.

seo.title: Privacy Policy · Awake Clock
seo.description: How Awake Clock handles your data: no accounts, no tracking, everything stays on your device.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Awake Clock is built to need as little of your data as possible. This page explains exactly what happens, and what does not.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Nothing. Awake Clock has no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking scripts. We don't know you visited, and we can't, because nothing is sent to a server.

sections.title: What's stored on your device
sections.body: Your preferences, such as theme, duration, clock template, and timer settings, are saved in your browser's local storage so they're there next time you visit. This data never leaves your device and is not accessible to us.

sections.title: The Screen Wake Lock
sections.body: Keeping your screen on uses your browser's built-in Screen Wake Lock API (or, on unsupported browsers, a silent looping video). Neither method reads, records, or transmits anything, it only tells your device not to sleep.

sections.title: Third-party services
sections.body: This site embeds a 'Buy Me a Coffee' support button, a third-party widget that may load resources from buymeacoffee.com. If you interact with it, your activity is subject to Buy Me a Coffee's own privacy policy, not ours.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
sections.body: If this policy changes, the update will be posted on this page. Continued use of the site after a change means you accept the update.

sections.title: Questions
